name: Bioacoustic Communication Membrane
description: Modifies the skin of the chest and upper back to function as a vibration-producing membrane capable of generating low-frequency acoustic signals — below normal hearing range but detectable by other Drum Skin users and by vibration-sensitive equipment. The signals can carry encoded information at ranges up to 50 meters through solid structures (floors, walls) and 20 meters through air. Users develop a haptic communication language — patterns of chest-vibration that convey words, emotions, and warnings. The modification was originally developed by Zheng-Dao Bioelectric for silent communication in secure environments. It has been adopted by the Shelf's courier networks, resistance cells, and any group that needs to communicate without being overheard. The vibrations are inaudible but can be felt by anyone in direct physical contact with the user — a hug becomes a conversation.
source_organism: Elephas maximus (Asian elephant, infrasonic communication), Heterocephalus glaber (naked mole rat, seismic communication)
procedure: Chest and back dermal modification with vibration-producing muscle fiber integration, 3 sessions
expression_time: 4–6 weeks; communication fluency requires months of practice with other users
reversibility: Muscle fiber modification reversible; skin modifications persist as slight textural change
side_effects: Involuntary vibration during emotional stress — broadcasting feelings to nearby users
Chest vibrations can be felt through thin furniture — unintentional communication leakage
Vibration production causes mild fatigue during extended communication
Other Drum Skin users can 'overhear' private vibration conversations within range
Rare: resonance with building structures causing audible hum that reveals communication
social_perception: Niche and secretive. Drum Skin users are part of a silent community that communicates beneath the threshold of normal perception. Non-users find the idea unsettling — conversations happening in their presence that they can't hear. The modification has a spy-craft reputation.
story_hooks: A Drum Skin user intercepts a vibration communication through a wall that describes a planned attack — they can't reveal how they know without exposing their own modification

A building's structure begins amplifying Drum Skin communications, turning private haptic conversations into audible hums that everyone can hear — someone has installed resonance amplifiers to expose the silent network
